descriptions.agent: Create a dedicated sub-agent to perform a specific task.
descriptions.ask_user_question:
Ask the user a question to get confirmation or a decision. Supports three types:
1. **choice** (default): closed multiple-choice with 2-4 fixed options. Use when options can be enumerated (e.g. "pick a tech stack").
2. **open**: open-ended confirmation where the user answers freely. Use when options cannot be enumerated (e.g. "what is your goal?").
3. **confirm**: yes/no confirmation. Use at decision points that require user approval (e.g. "continue execution?").

**Usage rules**:
- choice type: pass each option's label as a separate field; do not write it into the question text.
- open type: options may be an empty array or omitted; the system adds a free-input entry automatically.
- confirm type: options may be an empty array or omitted; the system generates "confirm/cancel" options automatically.
- The system appends an "Other" option at the end, allowing the user to enter free text.
descriptions.audio_play: Play audio files directly in the chat conversation. MUST call this after generating music/audio with music_generate to let users listen. Users cannot open file paths themselves — audio is only playable when you use this tool. Accepts local file paths or URLs. Supports audio playback with controls.
descriptions.bash:
Execute shell commands under safety checks.
The execution environment depends on the platform: on Windows it is cmd.exe (not bash; use \ for paths, dir/type/findstr/del/copy/move instead of ls/cat/grep/rm/cp/mv, %TEMP% for temporary files, and prefix complex scripts with powershell -Command "..."); on Unix it is /bin/sh.
descriptions.brief: Generate a summary of the current session.
descriptions.broadcast: Send a message to one or all channels. Supports single-channel delivery, broadcasting to all enabled channels, main-channel messages, and thread replies.
descriptions.browser: Automate Chrome to interact with web pages.
descriptions.browser_vision: Capture a screenshot of the current browser page and analyze it with vision AI. Returns the AI analysis and an optional screenshot path.
descriptions.canvas:
Create and manipulate visual canvases. Supports drawing shapes (rect, circle, line, path), text, image import, and exporting to PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG. Use when the user asks to create a diagram, draw on an image, add text annotations, or build a visual composition. Use create to start, then chain draw/text, and export to produce the final image.

Elements structure (each element in the "elements" array):
  - type: "rect"|"circle"|"line"|"text"|"image"|"path" (required)
  - x, y: position coordinates (required, number)
  - width, height: for rect/image (optional, number)
  - radius: for circle (optional, number)
  - fillColor, strokeColor: CSS color values (optional)
  - strokeWidth: line width (optional, number)
  - text: text content for text elements (optional)
  - fontSize: font size for text (optional, number, default 16)
  - opacity: 0.0-1.0 (optional)
  - points: array of {x,y} for line/path elements (optional)
Example: { type: "rect", x: 10, y: 20, width: 100, height: 50, fillColor: "#4A90D9" }
descriptions.channel: Unified channel management tool. List, connect, disconnect channels, check status, health, and view logs.
descriptions.clipboard: Read or write system clipboard content. Supports text operations across Windows, macOS, and Linux.
descriptions.code_run: Execute TypeScript orchestration code in a restricted sandbox. The code must not contain any import/require statements; capabilities are provided through the global __liriRuntime API (callTool/readContext/writeOutput/emitEvent/done). Call __liriRuntime.done(result) when finished. Use for complex multi-step tasks.
descriptions.computer_use: Desktop automation tool supporting Windows, macOS and Linux. Supports screenshot, mouse control, keyboard input, clipboard access, and window/application management.
descriptions.create_project: Create a new project for tracking complex tasks. Call when the user explicitly expresses intent to "create a project / manage tasks / track progress".
descriptions.create_task_list: Create multiple tasks at once. Use when the user provides a set of items to track as tasks (e.g. plan steps, to-dos). Input: a JSON array of task objects, each with a description and optional metadata.
descriptions.cron_create: Create a recurring or one-shot scheduled cron task. The task will execute at the specified schedule using the AI engine.
descriptions.cron_delete: Cancel/delete a scheduled cron task by ID
descriptions.cron_stop: Pause or resume a scheduled cron task by ID. Paused tasks will not fire until resumed.
descriptions.doc_generate: Create and populate Office documents (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx) or HTML pages (.html). Call this tool whenever the user asks to "create a document", "generate a weekly report", "write meeting minutes", "export as docx", or "export as html". Pass Markdown content (headings # ## ###, lists -, paragraphs, tables |) and a formatted document is generated automatically. When the content already exists in a local file (e.g. an html/md/txt document provided by the user), pass the content_file path instead of reciting long content — the tool reads the file directly, avoiding truncation and huge token usage. type defaults to docx; template options: weekly-report / meeting-minutes / tech-design / prd. Note: the output goes to the **global output directory** (~/.pyapp/output/); it does not belong to any project and is not registered in the Artifacts panel. If the document must be a project deliverable, use write_project_file to write it into that project's output/.
descriptions.enter_worktree: Create and switch to a git worktree to give the agent an isolated workspace and avoid polluting the main workspace.
descriptions.exit_worktree: Exit the git worktree and return to the original branch; optionally delete the worktree directory.
descriptions.file_convert: Convert file to Markdown format, or convert locally to .docx (no LLM involved). For local file conversion requests (e.g. html/md → Word), prefer this over doc_generate to avoid reciting long content through the model.Note: the output goes to the global output directory (~/.pyapp/output/); it does not belong to any project and is not registered in the Artifacts panel. If the file must be a project deliverable, use write_project_file to write it into that project's output/.
descriptions.file_write: Write content to a file. When the content already exists on disk (e.g. another tool produced a local file), you must pass source_file instead of reciting the full content as a string — this avoids output token explosion, JSON truncation, and memory bloat. Path resolution: absolute paths are used as-is; **relative paths / bare filenames resolve to the session working directory** (falling back to the global output directory `~/.pyapp/output/` only when there is no working directory). The receipt returns the **actual absolute path written** — use it when reporting the location, and do not rewrite it as `~/...` or another directory. If the file must be a project deliverable, use write_project_file to write it into that project's output/.
descriptions.get_task_list: Get the list of all current tasks with their ID, description, and status. Use to show the user their task list or to find a task ID for updates.
descriptions.glob: Find files matching a specified pattern.
descriptions.grep:
Powerful ripgrep-based search tool. Searches for specific text (via the pattern parameter) under a given directory.

Usage:
- Prefer grep for exact symbol / string searches; when conditions allow, use it instead of terminal grep/rg — it is faster and respects .gitignore.
- Full regex syntax is supported, e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+". Escape special characters when you need an exact match, e.g. "functionCall\("
- Supports filtering by file type and context lines.
- **Critical**: the directory must be an absolute path; relative paths are not accepted.
- **Critical**: the pattern parameter is required and must be given before other parameters.
- **Critical**: the directory parameter is named searchPath (the alias path is also accepted). Pass an absolute path, e.g. searchPath=/abs/path.
- headLimit: maximum number of result lines (default 200, must be a positive integer). Increase headLimit to retrieve more when output is truncated.
- The regex must be valid JS regex syntax, otherwise the tool degrades to a literal search and returns an invalidRegex hint. Use standard JS escapes: use [\u4e00-\u9fa5] for the Chinese range, not [\x{4e00}-\x{9fa5}] (the latter is invalid in JS regex and triggers degradation).
descriptions.image: Edit images with operations: resize, crop, rotate, flip, add watermark, adjust brightness/contrast/saturation, convert format, or grayscale. Use when the user asks to modify or transform an existing image.
descriptions.image_analysis: Analyze image content including metadata, colors, OCR text recognition, object detection, visual description (vision), and image similarity. Use when the user asks what is in an image, requests analysis, or needs to compare images. inputPath can be obtained from attachedImages or previous tool results.
descriptions.image_display: Display/preview images directly in the chat conversation. MUST call this after generating images with image_generate to show results to the user. Users cannot open file paths themselves — images are only visible when you use this tool. Accepts local file paths or URLs. Supports thumbnail grid, click-to-enlarge, and citation.
descriptions.image_generate: Generate AI images from text descriptions (prompts). Use this when the user asks to create, draw, or generate an image. Supports multiple aspect ratios, quality levels, and output formats. Returns file paths of generated images.
descriptions.image_svg_generate: Generate SVG vector graphics using LLM. Use when the user asks for icons, diagrams, logos, charts, UI elements, or simple illustrations. Supports multiple visual styles (flat, line, solid, colorful), custom colors, and background colors. Includes SVG syntax validation. Much cheaper than image generation APIs (text tokens only).
descriptions.knowledge_save: Save content to the user's knowledge base. Use when the user asks to save an article / web material / knowledge / archive content / remember something. Parameters: title + content. Once the save succeeds or the content already exists, the task is complete — confirm the result to the user and do not call this tool again.
descriptions.list_peers: Discover local peers (UDS socket) or remote sessions (bridge). Use to find agent processes you can connect to.
descriptions.list_vfs: List entries under an AI-VFS mount directory. Paths look like <scheme>://<authority>/<path>, e.g. dev_docs://配置与安全; calling with <scheme>:// (scheme-only, e.g. mcp://) lists the mounts under that scheme. Unregistered schemes fail explicitly and never fall back to the local filesystem.
descriptions.lsp: Language Server Protocol tool providing code intelligence: hover/definition/references/diagnostics/formatting/rename. When the target file is on disk (the vast majority of cases), prefer file_path over document — this avoids the model reciting thousands of lines of source, which causes output token explosion, JSON truncation, and context overflow.
descriptions.mcp_resource: List and read resources and prompts from connected MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers.
descriptions.mcp_tool: Connect to MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and use external tools. Supports stdio, SSE, WebSocket, and HTTP transports.
descriptions.music: Edit and manipulate audio/music files. Supports format conversion, metadata info, trimming, and volume adjustment.
descriptions.notebook: Notebook tool supporting creation, editing, and execution of mixed code and documents.
descriptions.pdf: Generate simple PDF documents from text content, or convert a local file directly to PDF. When the source content already exists on disk (e.g. a markdown/html/text file), you MUST pass content_file instead of reciting the full content — avoids output token explosion and long-content JSON truncation.Reading an existing PDF is NOT supported here: use file_read (auto-converted to Markdown) or media_pdf_extract instead.Note: the output goes to the global output directory (~/.pyapp/output/); it does not belong to any project and is not registered in the Artifacts panel. If this PDF must be a project deliverable, use write_project_file to write it into that project's output/.
descriptions.powershell: Execute PowerShell commands on Windows. Use for Windows-specific administration, registry operations, and system management.
descriptions.read_project_file: Read file contents in a project folder. Pass the project ID and a relative path; returns the file content. Only files inside the project sandbox can be read.
descriptions.read_vfs: Read file content from an AI-VFS mount. Paths look like <scheme>://<authority>/<path>, e.g. dev_docs://配置与安全/sandbox.md. Unregistered schemes fail explicitly and never fall back to the local filesystem.
descriptions.repl: Interactive programming environment supporting multiple languages.
descriptions.save_conversation: Save a conversation summary to a file. Use when the user wants to save or record the current conversation.
descriptions.sessions: Unified session management tool. List sessions, query status, view history, fork sessions, send messages, and delete sessions.
descriptions.sessions_yield: While delegated sub-agents are running, yield the current turn back to the session so their results can be awaited; the turn then continues with those results. This is the only tool that yields a turn — the `sessions` tool manages sessions and cannot yield.
descriptions.skill_view: Load a skill's full content by name. Use skills_list to see available skills.
descriptions.skills_list: List available skills (name + description). Use skill_view(name) to load the full content.
descriptions.sleep: Pause execution for a specified duration. Use when you need to wait before continuing (e.g. waiting for a resource, rate limiting, or timing).
descriptions.sleep_for: Suspend the current task and resume after N seconds. Short sleeps (<5 minutes) use an exact setTimeout; long sleeps use the CronScheduler tick.
descriptions.sleep_until: Suspend the current task until the specified ISO datetime.
descriptions.stat_vfs: Query metadata for a path in an AI-VFS mount (type / size / modified time / MIME / mount point / read-only). Paths look like dev_docs://配置与安全/sandbox.md.
descriptions.task_output: Get the output of a running or completed task by its ID.
descriptions.task_stop: Stop a running task by its ID.
descriptions.team_create: Create a new multi-agent swarm team to coordinate multiple agents on a task.
descriptions.team_delete: Disband a swarm team and clean up related resources.
descriptions.todo_write: Manage a to-do list to track tasks. Create, update, and complete to-do items.
descriptions.tool_search: Search for tools. When the tool you need is not in the current tool list (lazy-loaded, or hidden by this turn's task filtering), use this tool to search by keyword or "select:<tool_name>".
descriptions.trace_recording: Query AI API call traces and statistics. Retrieve recording status, stats, recent calls, and export trace data.
descriptions.tungsten: Manage terminal sessions (Tungsten). Create, list, switch, and manage interactive terminal sessions.
descriptions.update_task_status: Update a task's status by ID. Supported: pending, in_progress, completed, failed, cancelled.
descriptions.video: Edit and manipulate videos. Supports trim, compress, extract audio, format conversion, and metadata info.
descriptions.video_analysis: Analyze video content by extracting key frames and performing multi-level analysis (metadata → object detection → AI vision description). Supports mp4, webm, mov, avi, mkv, mpeg up to 50MB.
descriptions.video_display: Display/preview videos directly in the chat conversation. MUST call this after generating videos with video_generate to show results to the user. Users cannot open file paths themselves — videos are only visible when you use this tool. Accepts local file paths or URLs. Supports video playback with controls.
descriptions.video_generate: Generate videos using AI. Supports text-to-video and image-to-video via FAL.ai (Kling, Runway, MiniMax, etc.).
descriptions.web_fetch: Fetch content from a URL. Use to retrieve web page content, API responses, or other HTTP resources.
descriptions.web_search: Search the web for information. Use to find current events, facts, documentation, or any topic that needs up-to-date internet resources.
descriptions.write_project_file: Write a file into a project folder. Pass the project ID, a relative path, and the file content. AI outputs are saved to the project folder automatically. Only files inside the project sandbox can be written. When the content already exists in a local file (e.g. an md/html/docx/plan document the AI just generated), pass the source_file path instead of reciting long content — 0 output tokens, no truncation or memory blow-up.
descriptions.write_vfs: Write a file to an AI-VFS mount. Paths look like <scheme>://<authority>/<path>. If the mount is declared read-only (e.g. dev_docs://), it is explicitly rejected with VFS_READ_ONLY_MOUNT.
